en.title: Maximum Number of Password Segments Containing Both Vowels and Consonants
en.description:
Split the whole lowercase credential into non-empty contiguous segments; each segment must contain at least one vowel from aeiou and at least one other letter. The strength is the maximum number of segments; if the whole credential cannot satisfy both kinds of characters, return 0. Every character must be kept, so the tail cannot be discarded.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: One line containing credential. The original bounds are 1≤length≤10, with lowercase letters only. The corresponding raw is amazon-password-strength.md, not the other file with the same title, amazon-find-password-strength.md, which counts characters of substrings.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 3, 0 and 1. In the last example the suffix aaa joins the segment containing ab; the suffix is not discarded.
hints: Scan from the left; as soon as the current segment has collected both a vowel and a consonant, end it and start counting again. A tail at the end that cannot form a valid segment on its own joins the last valid segment and does not increase the count.
